title: ELF_IMEIJ.A_Backdoor_Investigation_c95
description: Investigate and respond to a potential compromise involving the ELF_IMEIJ.A backdoor on a target system.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has exhibited unusual network activity, suggesting a potential compromise. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. To begin, enter `start` in the passkey field.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. To begin, enter `start` in the passkey field.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: Investigate the target system for any unauthorized or suspicious services running. Identify the service that is potentially malicious.
levels.solution: Check the running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service is likely the one that is not part of the standard system services.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `systemctl status payload-transfer.service` to inspect the suspicious service.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after a system reboot. Identify the persistence mechanism used.
levels.solution: Examine systemd services and timers to find how the service is scheduled to run. The persistence mechanism is likely a systemd service or timer.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine systemd services and timers to find how the service is scheduled to run.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `systemctl status payload-transfer.timer` to inspect the persistence mechanism.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Identify the network port used for the suspicious communication between the target system and the potential command-and-control (C2) server.
levels.solution: Inspect network connections and logs to find the port used for outbound communication. The port used for the suspicious communication is likely the one that is not part of the standard system services.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Inspect network connections and logs to find the port used for outbound communication.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `ss -tulnp | grep 8080` to inspect the suspicious port.
